profile.summary: MIF (masked inverse folding) reads a protein's backbone structure together with a partly corrupted sequence and predicts the missing amino acids. It is a protein masked language model built as a structured graph neural network over the backbone. Its per-residue representations or amino acid predictions are used for protein engineering tasks such as variant effect prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: Abstract; README: Masked Inverse Folding (MIF) and Masked Inverse Folding with Sequence Transfer (MIF-ST)

summary_quotes.text: we train a masked inverse folding protein masked language model parameterized as a structured graph neural network.
this model learns to reconstruct corrupted sequences conditioned on the backbone structure.
We evaluate both of these models on downstream protein engineering tasks and analyze the effect of using information from experimental or predicted structures on performance.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is a masked language model built as a structured graph neural network that reconstructs corrupted sequences given the backbone. In the released loader it is a bidirectional Struct2Seq decoder with hidden size 256, four decoder layers and MPNN message passing, and each residue is joined to 30 neighbours. The structure reaches the network as inter-residue distances and the omega, theta and phi angles computed from the N, CA and C coordinates of a PDB file. For MIF the sequence enters as a one-hot encoding. MIF-ST, in the same repository, instead feeds in the outputs of CARP-640M.

sections.body: Zenodo record 6573779 (version 1.0, published 2022-05-23) holds mif.pt and mifst.pt, and a third file, mifgvp.pt, that the README does not describe. MIF is loaded by the name 'mif' and comes from mif.pt. The package is on PyPI as sequence-models, and the README also offers an install from the current main branch, so a result should name the package version or the commit used.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Masked inverse folding model: a protein masked language model conditioned on the backbone structure.

quotes.text: we train a masked inverse folding protein masked language model parameterized as a structured graph neural network.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Bidirectional Struct2Seq graph decoder with hidden size 256, four layers, MPNN message passing and 30 neighbours per residue; the sequence enters one-hot encoded.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A protein sequence with its backbone structure: N, CA and C coordinates parsed from a PDB file and turned into distances and dihedral angles. The bulk script reads a csv with name, sequence and pdb columns.

quotes.text: The input csv should have columns for `name`, `sequence`, and `pdb`.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-residue representations or per-residue amino acid logits. The bulk script can save per-token or mean embeddings, or an average log probability per sequence.

quotes.text: # can use result='repr' or result='logits'. Default is 'repr'.
`logp` computes the average log probability per sequence and stores it in a csv (only valid for logits).

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 3M trainable parameters, as listed in Table 1 of the S3F paper (Zhang, Notin and others, 2024), a later third-party evaluation. The developers' own sources read here state no count.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Not extracted. The journal full text is behind a robot check and was not read, and the sources read do not name the structure training set.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Two described checkpoints in Zenodo record 6573779: mif.pt and mifst.pt. A third file, mifgvp.pt, is in the record but not described in the README.

run_guide.summary: Install the package, load MIF with its weights from Zenodo and encode a protein from its PDB structure.
prerequisites: PyTorch. The README says the code was tested on versions 1.9.0, 1.11.0 and 1.12.
pandas, scipy and wget may need installing into a clean conda environment, as the README notes.
A CUDA device is optional for the bulk script and is detected automatically; the default is cpu.
Weights come from Zenodo record 6573779, declared there as bsd-license.

steps.title: Install the package
steps.explanation: The released package. The README also offers an install from the repository's main branch, which is not pinned.

steps.title: Get the repository at the pinned commit for the example files
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/protein-sequence-models.git
cd protein-sequence-models
git checkout --detach af695772c4a1c056d930c95ec7e6428aa042f5cd
steps.explanation: The README's commands read files under examples/. These clone and checkout lines are added to get them at the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Load MIF and encode one protein with its structure
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from sequence_models.pretrained import load_model_and_alphabet
from sequence_models.pdb_utils import parse_PDB, process_coords

model, collater = load_model_and_alphabet('mif')
coords, wt, _ = parse_PDB('examples/gb1_a60fb_unrelaxed_rank_1_model_5.pdb')
coords = {
        'N': coords[:, 0],
        'CA': coords[:, 1],
        'C': coords[:, 2]
    }
dist, omega, theta, phi = process_coords(coords)
batch = [[wt, torch.tensor(dist, dtype=torch.float),
          torch.tensor(omega, dtype=torch.float),
          torch.tensor(theta, dtype=torch.float), torch.tensor(phi, dtype=torch.float)]]
src, nodes, edges, connections, edge_mask = collater(batch)
rep = model(src, nodes, edges, connections, edge_mask)
print(rep.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README's snippets joined and wrapped in a shell heredoc, with the model name 'mif' from the README's list of available models. Three lines are added: the import of torch, which the README's snippet uses without importing, the import of load_model_and_alphabet from the README's own loading example, and a print of the output shape. The rest is the README's code. Loading downloads the weights from Zenodo.
